pairs.why: A's smooth, evenly lit pumpkin on plank wood matches the soft, clean finish of the real cards, while B's speckled skin leans toward the too-texture-y look the lessons reject.
B's slab with a recessed cross and soft grounded shadow reads like a believable stone object in the real cards' finish, while A's broken-top, raised-cross slab looks more like a waxy plastic toy.
B's ornate brass candelabra with dripping wax and warm glow matches the detailed, richly lit real oil lamp better than A's thin, plain stick-like build.
A is clearly built as a cratered rock with a soft matte finish like the real cards, while B is a shapeless purple blob with punched holes that doesn't read as a real meteor.
A's chunky, softly glossy console with readable gauges and buttons has the real cards' lighting and appeal, while B is a flat, pastel cabinet with dull, low-contrast shading.

A's rounded orange vehicle with headlights, glass and crisp highlights shares the real taxi's rendering and color punch, while B's matte clay-like box with plain blob wheels looks duller and more toy-like.
B's saturated orange body and clean smooth surfaces fit the real cards' bright palette, while A's white-grey rover on gritty grey moon ground is drab and more texture-heavy.
B's glossy orange vehicle with headlights and window matches the real taxi's color and finish, while A's white box on gritty grey ground looks drab and over-textured.
